title: Nithya Raman Takes 11-Point Lead Over Karen Bass Into Only LA Mayoral Debate
excerpt: A Berkeley IGS/Los Angeles Times poll puts the Indian-American councilmember ahead 39% to 28% — but with 33% of voters undecided and mail ballots already out, the October 14 debate is the race's biggest moment.
body:
• Indian-American Councilmember Nithya Raman leads Mayor Karen Bass 39% to 28% among likely voters in a UC Berkeley IGS/Los Angeles Times poll, heading into the race's only live televised debate on October 14.
  • A third of likely voters — 33% — are still undecided, and the poll of 2,150 voters (September 15-20, margin of error about 3 points) was taken before mail ballots went out.
  • Among Latino voters, Raman's lead widens to 45% against 21% for Bass, with 34% undecided — a decisive bloc in a city where Latinos routinely make up roughly a quarter of turnout.
  • Key dates for LA voters: the debate is October 14, mail ballots are already in voters' hands, and the runoff election is November 3.

Los Angeles Councilmember Nithya Raman faces Mayor Karen Bass on October 14 in the only live televised debate of the mayoral race, carrying an 11-point lead from the latest independent polling — and a warning inside the same numbers: a third of the electorate has not made up its mind. The UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies poll, co-sponsored by the Los Angeles Times, put Raman at 39% among likely voters to Bass's 28%, with 33% undecided, according to IANS. The online survey of 2,150 likely voters ran September 15-20 with a margin of error of about 3 percentage points.

How the race got here

Raman and Bass were longtime allies until Raman entered the race on the last day of filing in February — weeks after publicly endorsing Bass — saying the city "can't seem to manage the basics." She placed second behind Bass in the June primary, ahead of former reality TV star Spencer Pratt; most Pratt voters have not chosen a runoff candidate, a key reason the undecided share is so high. Homelessness, housing affordability, public safety, economic development and preparations for the 2028 Olympics are expected to dominate the debate, LAist reported. Bass has dismissed the poll, saying she does not see Raman as the frontrunner.

The fight has turned sharp

The contest has turned bitter over the police department. After Raman appeared in a since-deleted social media video featuring the words "Only you can stop fascist liars," Bass called her "incredibly irresponsible" and questioned whether she is ready to lead the city. Raman, born in India and brought to the US at age six, was elected to the City Council in 2020 and represents the 4th District, including Hollywood, Sherman Oaks and Van Nuys. Her campaign has centred on dissatisfaction with City Hall's handling of homelessness and basic services — a message she says a third of voters share.

Why the Latino numbers matter

The poll's cross-tabs explain the campaigns' endgame. Among Latino likely voters, Raman leads 45% to 21%, though 34% remain undecided — and the age split cuts the other way for older Latino voters, who lean to Bass. With mail ballots already delivered and three weeks to Election Day, the single debate is the largest shared audience either campaign will get to move those undecided blocs.

What's next

The debate airs October 14; the runoff is November 3. For Indian-American voters in Los Angeles — one of the largest diaspora concentrations in the US — the race offers something rare: a co-ethnic candidate leading an incumbent mayor of America's second-largest city, with the outcome riding on voters who have not yet decided.
